samples.request: Please look for all the files that end with the .md extension, then for each one count how many lines talk about 'auth' and rank the files from the most mentions to the fewest. samples.output:
<function=run_nushell>
<parameter=code>
glob **/*.md | each {|p| $p | path relative-to (pwd)} | where ($it | path type) == file | par-each {|f| {file: $f, hits: (open --raw $f | lines | where ($it | str contains -i 'auth') | length)} } | where hits > 0 | sort-by file | sort-by hits --reverse | to json --raw
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
samples.code: glob **/*.md | each {|p| $p | path relative-to (pwd)} | where ($it | path type) == file | par-each {|f| {file: $f, hits: (open --raw $f | lines | where ($it | str contains -i 'auth') | length)} } | where hits > 0 | sort-by file | sort-by hits --reverse | to json --raw

samples.request: List what is in **logs**; then return their **names**; then keep the last 1; then report status not_found, resolved (with file) or choose_one (with matches). Return it as JSON. Part for the whole (names only one or two of the things involved while meaning all of them). These must appear in your rewrite exactly as written: 1, logs.
samples.output:
<function=run_nushell>
<parameter=code>
let matches = (ls logs | get name | sort); let result = (if ($matches | is-empty) { {status: 'not_found'} } else if (($matches | length) > 1) { {status: 'choose_one', matches: $matches} } else { {status: 'resolved', file: ($matches | first)} }); $result | to json --raw
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
samples.code: let matches = (ls logs | get name | sort); let result = (if ($matches | is-empty) { {status: 'not_found'} } else if (($matches | length) > 1) { {status: 'choose_one', matches: $matches} } else { {status: 'resolved', file: ($matches | first)} }); $result | to json --raw
